Map tiles blocked in this preview

This interactive map renders fully when deployed to GitHub Pages or opened locally. All crash data, markers, corridors, and tools are loaded — they just need a basemap.

Not on the map: 6,072 of 151,463 crashes (4.0%) have no usable coordinates in the CDOT records. They are counted in every total and chart on this page.

About this map and your privacy

Privacy: This page has no backend, no analytics, and no cookies, and nothing you type is stored by crashmaps. Loading it fetches fonts from Google Fonts, scripts from cdnjs (Cloudflare) and map tiles from CARTO, and each of those services sees your IP address. An address you search is sent to OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and commute start and end points are sent to the public OSRM routing server. Those requests are subject to each service’s privacy policy.

12 — Vision ZeroVision Zero

Vision Zero: Progress Toward Zero

The City and County of Denver adopted Vision Zero in 2017, setting a target of 0 traffic deaths by 2030. The baseline was 51 deaths in 2017. The chart counts deaths in the City and County of Denver only; the other sections of this dashboard cover the wider metro.

13 — Sources

Where This Data Comes From

CDOT Crash Listing
Crash records from the Colorado Department of Transportation Statewide Crash Listing. 49,021 records for 2025, covering 17 city groups in the Denver metro area.

CDOT Crash Data →
Denver Vision Zero
Denver adopted Vision Zero in 2017, committing to eliminate traffic fatalities and serious injuries by 2030.

Vision Zero Denver →
14 — Methodology

How I Built This

Data pipeline: CDOT Statewide Crash Listing Excel files parsed via Python adapter. Records filtered to the six metro counties (Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, Jefferson). 49,021 records for 2025.
City assignment: The CDOT City field maps crashes to 17 metro city groups. When City is blank (common on sheriff and State Patrol reports), the city is assigned from the crash coordinates using official DOLA municipal boundaries; crashes outside every municipality go to their county’s catch-all city group.
Behavioral flags: DUI from alcohol/marijuana/drug suspected fields. Speed from contributing factor text and speed-over-limit detection (>10 mph over). Hit-and-run from TU hit-and-run boolean fields. Pedestrian and cyclist from crash type text.

Data: CDOT Crash Data · Vision Zero Denver · CDOT
